text:
incident-bot: PAGER — SEV2: detected SLO breach on prod-inference. p99 decode latency = 1.8s (SLO 1.0s). Affected route(s): /v1/generate-stream. Paging eng-oncall.

sara: ACK. I'm oncall and grabbing dashboards.

sara: quick read — p95 ~0.42s, p99 ~1.8s for decode step only. Streaming stalls reported by a few customers (clients receive tokens then pause ~700–1200ms).

leo: linking traces and flamegraphs: https://grafana.example/trace/abcd1234 and https://profiler.example/flame/ef56

maria: any infra changes in last 24h?

maria: I see infra-toolchain deploy at 2026-03-12T22:10:03Z (tag infra-toolchain@v2.3.0).

kiran: FYI there was a merge yesterday that bumped FlashAttention and updated TensorRT/compile flags (PR #4578).

sara: running quick diffs to find build-time flags.

sara: ```bash
# list toolchain flags
git show infra-toolchain@v2.3.0 --name-only --pretty=oneline
grep -n "FLASHATTN|USE_TRT|VECTORIZE" -n build/configs/*.cmake || true
```

sara: grep shows `-DUSE_FLASHATTN=ON` and `-DCOMPILE_WITH_TRT=1` added in that tag.

tim: logs from a sample decode on a hot node show attention kernel time jumping from ~0.12ms/token to ~0.9ms/token for short sequences. Attaching snippet:```
[2026-03-13 02:08:21] decode: attention_forward kernel time: 0.9ms (was 0.12ms)
[2026-03-13 02:08:21] memcpy H2D: 0.05ms, D2H: 0.04ms
[2026-03-13 02:08:21] kv-cache hit ratio unchanged
```

leo: nvprof summary shows a spike in kernel launch overhead and more small kernels (FlashAttn path). Might be kernel fragmentation + scheduler overhead on our GPU instance type.

sara: immediate mitigation attempt — try disabling new FlashAttention path on a canary pool to confirm. Command I'm applying to canary config: set env REDWOOD_DISABLE_FLASHATTN=1 for decode service.

infra-ci: rolling canary: deploying env change to 3 nodes in us-west-2 (pool: decode-canary-g5).

sara: canary metrics updated: within 3 minutes p99 dropped from 1.8s -> 0.95s on nodes with REDWOOD_DISABLE_FLASHATTN=1. p95 unchanged.

leo: good signal. This indicates new kernel path (FlashAttn / TRT flags) is regressing tail latency for streaming workloads with short sequences.

maria: drafting customer note. Should we inform customers now or after partial mitigation?

sara: recommend limited customer message: "We're investigating a latency regression affecting streaming. We've applied a mitigation and are rolling it to more capacity. Some customers may see shorter pauses temporarily." I'll push to top 10 accounts.

kiran: remediation plan: 1) expand env flag to all prod routing nodes, 2) revert toolchain tag infra-toolchain@v2.3.0 in build pipeline, 3) run instrumented branch to pinpoint kernel hotpaths. I'll own the revert PR.

tim: creating revert branch and smoke tests. Revert PR queued as revert-pr/4578-revert-flashattn.

infra-ci: initiating staged rollout of REDWOOD_DISABLE_FLASHATTN=1 to 50% traffic (step increase). Expected completion ~6min.

sara: monitoring: at 50% rollout p99 aggregated dropped to ~1.05s. No increase in error rate or request failures. Streaming stalls greatly reduced per synthetic clients.

nate: I'm stepping in for the next 2 hours to watch the rollout and follow up on the revert. Handoff: @sara, status?

sara: handing to @nate. Current: mitigation env flag at 50%, canary validated, p99 trending down. Rollout continuing to 100% after we confirm metrics stable for 10 more minutes.

kiran: I'll open an incident ticket and attach the PRs, traces, and metric snapshots. Root-cause hypothesis: the new toolchain enabled an alternate FlashAttention kernel path and/or different compiler vectorization that has worse tail latency for short-sequence streaming. Needs deeper kernel-level profiling.

tim: smoke tests for revert in CI passed. Queueing revert to prod image builder.

infra-ci: full rollout of mitigation flag (100% traffic) initiated — expected impact window 8–10 minutes.

sara: metrics after full rollout: p99 stabilized ~0.98s and p95 0.40s. No customer error spike.

maria: customer comms sent to top 10 accounts and status channel.

kiran: post-incident actions: (a) make kernel microbenchmarks for both FlashAttn and fallback kernels across sequence lengths 8/32/128, (b) add automated regression tests to CI that assert p99 thresholds for short-sequence streaming, (c) investigate compiler flags that changed vectorization patterns.

nate: I'll run the extended microbench overnight and post results here tomorrow morning.

tim: postmortem ticket created: INCD-2026-89 (assigned to eng-runtime + infra).

kiran: owners: kiran (infra), leo (runtime), nate (bench + follow-up).

sara: severity confirmed SEV2. Customer impact = performance degradation only (latency), no failed requests. Mitigation executed successfully. Handoff complete.

incident-bot: Incident closed (mitigated). Duration ~45m. Reference: INCD-2026-89.

sara: closing notes: keep the revert PR prioritized until we can identify a safe FlashAttn upgrade with acceptable tail behavior. Postmortem to include graphs (p95/p99 before/after), deployment diffs, and concrete CI gates. :white_check_mark:
